meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Roman-Dutch common law overlain by English common-law procedural heritage with constitutional supremacy under the Constitution, 1996; uncodified private law combined with a statutory company law and AML/CFT code.

SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006)
Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA, in force 2021)

Bilateral Investment Treaty: South Africa - China (1998)
Double Taxation Agreements in force: US (1997), UK (2002), India (1997), Netherlands (2001), Australia (1999), Mauritius (2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Acts 16 and 17 of 2024; Companies Regulations 2011 (GNR 351 of 28 April 2011) read with the Companies Amendment Regulations 2023; FIC Guidance Note 7 (Beneficial Ownership), FIC Guidance Note 3A, FIC Directive 5, and Cabinet-approved FIC Guidance Note 4 (Politically Exposed Persons); Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution or municipal utility authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin followed by Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization for non-Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign banking institution holding the account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (i) the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions lists (UNSCR 1267/1989 and 1373 regime); (ii) the South African domestic terrorism proscription list administered under Act 33 of 2004; (iii) the OFAC SDN List and EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions as a prudential correspondent-banking standard; (iv) FATF public statements and grey/black-list jurisdiction indicators. PEP classification must follow FICA s.21A and Cabinet-approved FIC Guidance Note 4, including capture of family members and close associates, with a minimum 12-month cooling-off review after cessation of public office. Enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification is required for high-risk jurisdictions and any negative screening hit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC BizPortal (https://bizportal.cipc.co.za) and CIPC e-Services, Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be filed in the Latin alphabet; a non-Latin-script foreign name (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be rendered in an English transliteration. The name may be drawn from any of the 11 official South African languages, but under Companies Act s.11(2)-(5) it must not be offensive, defamatory, imply state, royal, or university patronage, or conflict with a protected trademark or earlier-registered company name. The mandatory suffix for a private company is 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The pipeline-standard validity window is 30 days; a lapsed reservation is not extended by CIPC as of course, and the applicant should file a fresh reservation application via BizPortal. Upon rejection, the applicant's primary remedy is expedited re-filing of a revised distinguishable name supported by a mark-similarity explanation. The secondary remedy is a statutory review: an application under s.160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 to the Companies Tribunal, delivered within the prescribed period (generally 15 business days under the Companies Tribunal Rules, 2011), with simultaneous service on CIPC, seeking an order directing CIPC to reserve or register the name. Strict compliance with the Tribunal's filing rules and payment of any prescribed filing fee is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this low-risk wholesale optical-frames distribution activity only if it consists of a physical serviced office in South Africa with a genuine street address, attended reception during ordinary business hours, mail capture, and process-service capacity as required by s.23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. A digital-only virtual address, P.O. Box, or pure mail-forwarding arrangement does not satisfy the statutory registered-office or FICA accountable-institution substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-negligible: approximately 3% estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by CIPC, the Financial Intelligence Centre, or SARS for a non-licensed, low-risk wholesale trader with a clean record. The probability increases to above 25% where a suspicious transaction report, a SARS audit trigger, or a FATF grey-list compliance inspection arises; South Africa remains under enhanced FATF monitoring as of 2025.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account required. At least one share must be issued and the share particulars set out in the MOI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in, submit a name reservation application with at least three proposed names in order of preference, pay the prescribed fee, and obtain a name reservation for 20 business days (renewable).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh reservation with alternate names; appeals or objections are filed with CIPC’s Name Tribunal within 2 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI adopting the Companies Act’s standard provisions or incorporating bespoke provisions. Each initial incorporator must sign the MOI; no notarization is required for domestic filings.
required_dossiers: Consent letters from first directors and company secretary if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the MOI in line with CIPC’s document standards and resubmit; if conflict with Companies Act mandatory provisions, the conflicting provision is void and must be reworded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Notice of Incorporation and Pay Registration Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1), attach the signed MOI and supporting consents, select registration fee, and submit. CIPC issues a registration certificate and company number upon final approval.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of identity documents of directors/incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a compliance query or correction notice, respond within 20 business days by correcting the relevant form or MOI and resubmitting; late response causes withdrawal of the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax and UIF with SARS and Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: CIPC automatically registers the company with SARS for income tax. The company must further register for VAT if annual taxable turnover exceeds the threshold, register as an employer for PAYE/UIF and apply for a tax clearance.
required_dossiers: Company details and SARS reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS flags incomplete particulars, file the missing documents via eFiling or visit a SARS branch; tax clearance can be applied for once all returns are up to date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local metropolitan or district municipality; Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the business with the local municipality for trading rights, apply for an occupancy certificate for the registered office/warehouse, and, if importing frames, register with SARS Customs for an importer code.
required_dossiers: Certificate of occupancy or approved building plans
Fire certificate from the local fire authority
SARS Customs importer registration form if importing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires additional building or fire safety conditions, complete the corrective work and resubmit the certificate; customs importer registrations may be queried by SARS and resolved via eFiling messaging.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for wholesale distribution; no industrial licensing board permit is required. National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) may set product safety standards for eyewear frames, but does not license the business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; a SARS Customs importer code is mandatory for imported frames, but no separate operating permit is issued for wholesale optical frame distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – warehouse and commercial office use does not trigger listed activities under the EIA Regulations, 2014; no environmental authorisation required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions; domestic sewage to municipal sewer under municipal by-laws; packaging and waste handling must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 (section 19).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Compliance Certificate from the local fire protection service; structural load clearance for racking under the National Building Regulations; Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 workplace compliance and registration with the Department of Employment and Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); electronic portal: SARS eFiling at https://efiling.sars.gov.za; company registration portal: CIPC BizPortal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a local (Pty) Ltd with foreign shareholders, incorporate with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) through CIPC/BizPortal using a Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation. CIPC data is linked to SARS and an income tax reference number is usually created automatically. If not auto-registered, file income tax registration through SARS eFiling within 21 days. File VAT/VAT vendor registration using VAT 101/ACC01 through SARS eFiling, together with the CIPC registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, directors' identity documents, and proof of physical address in South Africa. For a branch of a foreign company, register as an external company with CIPC, then register with SARS and appoint a local authorised representative. SARS will issue a taxpayer reference number and, where taxable supplies exceed the threshold, a VAT vendor number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable – South Africa has no U.S.-style check-the-box election; a (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily a separate taxable company under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962. Available targeted elections include the Headquarter Company election under section 9I for qualifying multinational holding companies, the research-and-development allowance election under section 11D, and certain roll-over reliefs under sections 41-47 (e.g. asset-for-share, amalgamation) where a joint election is filed. No hybrid-mismatch check-the-box election is available; hybrid debt/equity instruments are statutorily reclassified under sections 8F, 8FA and 23M.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted from ZAR 50,000 of taxable supplies. A non-resident supplying electronic services to South African customers must register for VAT if total taxable supplies from such services exceed ZAR 1,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate is in force in South Africa. Tax invoices must satisfy section 20 of the VAT Act (supplier name and VAT number, invoice number, date, description, quantity, price and VAT amount); electronic tax invoices are valid if the integrity and readability of the invoice are preserved. VAT returns are filed electronically through SARS eFiling using VAT 201 returns on a monthly or two-monthly cycle, with SARS automated risk/audit referral and no statutory requirement for a pre-clearance API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from South Africa are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the supplier exports the goods in the ordinary course of its trade, the goods are removed to a foreign destination within the prescribed time period (usually within 90 days), and the supplier retains documentary proof of export. Services supplied to non-residents and consumed wholly outside South Africa may be zero-rated under section 11(2)(l). A wholesale exporter of acetate eyeglass frames must hold a completed SARS Customs export declaration (SAD500), transport documents evidencing physical removal from SACU, and proof of payment or foreign-currency receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged on SARS Customs
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (where export proceeds are received through authorised foreign-exchange channels from outside South Africa)
Proof of receipt of export proceeds (bank inward/swift credit advice)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict SARS audit scrutiny. Where export conditions are not met, SARS may re-assess the supply at 15% VAT with statutory interest and claw back input tax previously deducted. Failure to produce prescribed export documentation exposes the vendor to input/output VAT disallowance, understatement penalties under section 223 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 (up to 200% depending on conduct), administrative non-compliance penalties, and criminal sanctions where zero-rating is claimed fraudulently. SARS may raise a revised assessment beyond the ordinary five-year prescription period where fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the delegated Exchange Control authority, together with Authorised Dealers (domestic commercial banks duly appointed under the Currency and Exchanges Act, No. 9 of 1933, and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a dual-tier exchange control framework. The current account—including wholesale importation and distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames, professional fees, and trade-related service payments—is effectively convertible for residents and non-residents, subject to documentary substantiation, arm's-length pricing, and adherence to prescribed reporting requirements. The capital account is controlled. Non-resident equity investments into a South African company are admissible through Authorised Dealers with streamlined notification for ordinary share capital, but disinvestment and share buy-backs require tax directives from SARS and may require FinSurv approval where thresholds apply. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted provided the dividends are paid out of verified after-tax profits, the company is fully tax compliant, and the remittance is effected through an Authorised Dealer using the prescribed Form A.2. Profit remittances are not subject to exchange-control approval for ordinary dividend flows, but any payment that represents hidden capital or interest on shareholder loans must be separately assessed and may trigger transfer-pricing review under Section 31 of the Income Tax Act, No. 58 of 1962.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: This entity's primary trade flow is importation and domestic wholesale distribution of eyeglass frames; therefore, the statutory surrender regime is not triggered unless the company subsequently re-exports frames. For any future export transactions, a South African resident exporter must surrender foreign currency proceeds to an Authorised Dealer within 30 days of shipment or by the contractual payment due date, whichever is earlier, and must convert or credit the full amount into rand or an approved Foreign Currency Account within 30 days of receipt. There is no prescribed minimum conversion ratio because all foreign currency received without special approval must be sold to an Authorised Dealer or retained only in a FinSurv-approved Foreign Currency Account. A 100% mandatory conversion is therefore the operational baseline; exceptions require a formal exchange-control application and specific approval. The exporter must also complete and submit the applicable Form B.1 or digital equivalent, retain supporting shipping and customs documentation, and report all export proceeds on the Authorised Dealer's periodic exchange-control return.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Share Subscription Account and Operational Current ZAR Account with Authorised Dealer forex capability
Operational ZAR Account and Trade Finance / Import Settlement Account under Authorised Dealer licence

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g. Wise, Airwallex, and comparable non-bank providers) do not hold South African banking licences and are not permitted to operate local ZAR clearing or to maintain nostro accounts in South Africa unless separately authorised by SARB as an Authorised Payment Institution (API) or an Authorised Dealer with limited authority. For an entity seeking to import capital and settle trade payments in compliance with Exchange Control Regulations, reliance on an unlicensed offshore EMI is legally vulnerable and operationally inadequate. Such platforms may only be used as payment initiation tools to the extent that funds are ultimately routed through a licensed Authorised Dealer; direct ZAR treasury management and statutory exchange-control reporting must remain with tier-1 domestic commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, No. 38 of 2001 (FICA), banks must perform identity, fraud, and customer due diligence assessments, including beneficial ownership verification. There is no absolute statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically in South Africa; however, in practice, for a private company with non-resident shareholders, most tier-1 banks require at least one director or an appointed authorised representative to complete an in-person verification interview at the bank's South African branch or a notary equivalent. Remote account opening is possible where the bank's automated e-KYC process is accepted, but any account that requires exchange-control approval—particularly a Capital Escrow / Share Subscription Account—cannot be opened entirely remotely. The bank will require certified copies of passport pages, board resolutions, memorandum of incorporation, a local registered office address, proof of the directors' residential addresses (not older than three months), and independent verification of the extract from the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) opacity: any shareholder who is not a natural person or where natural persons cannot be identified on the final ownership layer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration signed by each director; corporate organisational chart connecting the entity to every natural person holding more than 25% of ownership or control; certified passport copies and proof of residence of natural persons; independent sanction and adverse-media screening reports; notarised board resolution confirming ownership structure; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; and an explanatory memorandum describing the commercial rationale for the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection into the South African company that appears structured as a shareholder loan rather than genuine equity, or that is not accompanied by supporting exchange-control documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreement clearly labelled as equity; payment instruction from the shareholder's own bank account with no interposition of third-party funds; certified SWIFT MT103 credit advice reflecting the exact purpose code for foreign direct investment; a Form A.2 or Form B.1 (as applicable) submitted through the Authorised Dealer; the bank's inward transfer notification; SARS tax clearance certificate for the entity; valuation report or independent confirmation of issue price where shares are issued for non-cash assets; and board minutes resolving the allotment of shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Imported ophthalmic eyewear frames suspected to be subject to transfer-pricing manipulation or under/over-invoicing, particularly where invoice prices differ materially from market value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice and pro forma invoice from the offshore supplier; arm's-length price benchmarks from international industry databases or published competitor price lists; full import documentation including bills of lading, packing lists, and customs declarations; supplier contracts; intercompany pricing policy; transfer-pricing documentation prepared under Section 31 of the Income Tax Act, No. 58 of 1962; and the entity's customs duty and VAT declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media matches on counterparties, or transactions routed through high-risk jurisdictions without adequate economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Integrated sanctions screening report at counterparty and beneficial owner level; transaction-specific rationale and final destination/use analyses; enhanced due diligence questionnaire covering source of funds and end-use; attestation from the company's chief compliance officer; independent legal opinion mapping the transaction to applicable UN, EU, US OFAC, and South African sanctions frameworks; and documentary proof of the counterparty's physical presence and legitimate trade history.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route for inbound equity capital from a non-resident shareholder is as follows: (1) Execute the share subscription agreement between the company and the non-resident shareholder. (2) Instruct the chosen Authorised Dealer (South African Tier 1 bank) to open a Capital Escrow / Share Subscription Account where funds are held pending allotment of shares. (3) The shareholder must remit funds via SWIFT MT103 from its own corporate or personal bank account using the purpose code 'equity participation in South African private company' or the equivalent SARB declaration code; the remitter must be the subscribing shareholder and no third-party payments are acceptable. (4) The Authorised Dealer verifies the source of funds, scans for sanctions exposure, and completes the exchange-control Form A.2 (notification of inward investment). (5) After the bank receives the funds, the company files the necessary share allotment documents with CIPC, issues beneficial share certificates, and records the inward investment in the company's register of shareholders. (6) The Authorised Dealer captures the transaction on FinSurv's reporting system; a Foreign Investment Approval / Notarial Letter or equivalent is issued for the company's records. If the inward investment is not classified as equity, for example because the subscribing entity is a resident or the funds are intended as a loan, it cannot be routed through this lane and would require a separate exchange-control application or be refused.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment of imports of ophthalmic eyewear frames and related wholesale trade disbursements, the company must use an Authorised Dealer in accordance with Exchange Control Regulations. The standard clearing rails are: (1) a direct outward SWIFT MT103 remittance for ordinary trade settlements, initiated by the company's ZAR operational account and converted into the invoiced foreign currency; (2) a documentary commercial letter of credit (L/C) where the overseas supplier requires irrevocable payment security, established by the bank on behalf of the company; and (3) documentary collections (D/P or D/A) through the bank's trade services channel. Every record of payment must be supported by the original/pro forma commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and customs clearance documentation. The company is also required to obtain and maintain an Import Permit / Exchange Control Form A.1 (or the relevant digital equivalent) filed with the Authorised Dealer. Payments to non-resident suppliers cannot be made from an account other than that which is approved by the Authorised Dealer; settlement of open account trade must occur within the agreed credit period and may be extended only with prior approval where financing is required. All SWIFT messages must use accurate ISO purpose codes for goods imports, and the bank is responsible for monthly reporting of each trade transaction to FinSurv.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Direct deliverable ZAR/foreign-currency forwards transacted with an Authorised Dealer for periods up to 12 months, supported by an underlying current-account transaction, without prior SARB approval.
Cross-currency swaps on the spot and forward market for trade-related cash flow management, subject to the Authorised Dealer's internal limits and FinSurv reporting for any tenors exceeding 12 months

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore by the non-resident shareholder or counterparty; onshore South African corporates do not typically use NDFs as a treasury standard and such instruments are permitted only in exceptional circumstances with express FinSurv approval where an underlying exposure exists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (AR) filing and confirmation of company details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of ZAR 500 per annum; continued non-compliance may lead to deregistration or administrative strike-off by CIPC after due process

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (AFS) preparation and filing (where required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (for public and state-owned companies; private companies may file exemption notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end for public/state-owned entities; private companies must file annual return and, if required, AFS within the same CIPC annual return window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of ZAR 500 per annum for late annual return; failure to file AFS where mandated may result in compliance notice and potential referral to enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Return (ITR14 or applicable corporate return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 12 months after the company's financial year-end (assessment date assigned by SARS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of up to 10% of assessed tax per month of non-compliance; SARS may issue an estimated assessment and pursue collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Turnover tax or VAT return (if registered for VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Bi-monthly or annually as per SARS registration category; annual small business VAT return due within 21 days after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of unpaid tax plus interest at prescribed rate; failure to file may trigger criminal prosecution for repeat non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Applicable from 1 April 2023 for existing companies; confirmation required on each annual return within 30 business days of anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalty of up to ZAR 1,000 per month for non-compliance; directors/company may be subject to enforcement measures including strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit compulsory for public companies, state-owned companies, and any company whose public interest score is 350 or greater; also required if the company is regulated by a sector-specific regulator requesting an audit or if its Articles of Association mandate an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for public interest score above 350 or public/state-owned; IFRS for SMEs permitted for qualifying smaller private companies; local GAAP (South African GAAP) applies to entities not using IFRS and not qualifying for IFRS for SMEs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On each annual return, the company must confirm its beneficial ownership register is accurate and up to date; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change, and the annual confirmation must reflect the updated register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 for a private company with no public interest score; USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 for larger or higher-risk companies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential Small Business Corporation (SBC) rates apply if turnover ≤ ZAR 20 million, shareholders are natural persons only, and gross income ≤ ZAR 20 million: 0% on first ZAR 95,000; 7% on next ZAR 95,000; 21% on next ZAR 190,000; 27% above ZAR 380,000. Additional deductions: s11(a) general deduction; s11D 150% R&D allowance; s12C capital allowances (20%/40%); s12H learnership allowance; s10(1)(k) participation exemption for foreign dividends (≥10% shareholding); s6quat(1) foreign tax credit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed statutory limit; assessed losses carry forward indefinitely, subject to the s20A annual cap of the greater of ZAR 1 million or 80% of taxable income before loss set-off

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 - Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically via SARS eFiling (efiling.sars.gov.za)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the financial year-end (year of assessment). For a 28/29 February year-end, due on or before the following 28/29 February; for any other year-end (e.g., 31 March), due on the last day of the same month in the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All amounts received by or accrued to the company from wholesale sales of acetate eyeglass frames, excluding exempt income; includes platform payment settlements and Swift TT receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: ZA resident company declares worldwide income; a non-resident carrying on trade in South Africa through a permanent establishment declares only South African-source income attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempt under s10, including certain dividends and foreign dividends qualifying for the participation exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident claims exemptions only where specifically granted in the Income Tax Act or an applicable DTA (e.g., international shipping and aircraft income).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses actually incurred in the production of income: cost of inventory, freight, customs duties, warehousing, selling and administrative expenses, depreciation, and allowable amortisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE deducts expenses incurred for the purposes of the South African PE, supported by contemporaneous records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Section 20 assessed loss from prior years, limited each year to the greater of ZAR 1 million or 80% of taxable income (s20A).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only where the non-resident has a South African permanent establishment with a preceding assessed loss; otherwise left blank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less exempt income, deductions, and allowable assessed loss set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident computes the same on South African-source PE income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable normal tax on taxable income at the 27% corporate rate (or SBC progressive rates where eligible).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same rate applies to the taxable income of a non-resident PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary rebates, s6quat foreign tax credits, provisional tax payments (IRP6), and PAYE where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit claimed only where the applicable DTA assigns taxing rights to South Africa or where s6quat conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net normal tax after credits; any balance due must be paid electronically by the due date to avoid s213 penalty and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident must settle any balance through the eFiling payment channels using a South African bank account or approved cross-border payment rail.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: s210 TAA administrative non-compliance penalty for late filing: category-based monthly amounts (up to ZAR 2,000 per month and maximum 35 months); s213 late payment penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax; s222 understatement penalties of 10%, 25%, 50% or 75% depending on the degree of culpability; interest at the prescribed rate (repo rate + 350 bps); criminal prosecution under s234/s235 TAA for fraudulent returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 - Provisional Tax Estimation and Payment Return; filed and paid via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with two mandatory provisional payments and one voluntary third payment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional payment: within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment (e.g., 31 August for a 1 March - 28/29 February tax year). Second provisional payment: on or before the last day of the year of assessment (e.g., 28/29 February). Voluntary third payment: within 6 months after year-end (e.g., 31 August).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reasonable estimate of taxable income for the current year of assessment based on gross margin and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident with a SA PE estimates income attributable to the PE; no return if no SA trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry-in of assessed loss estimated for the year, subject to s20A limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable unless the non-resident has a SA PE with loss history.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable normal tax on the estimated taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same calculation applies to PE taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits expected to be available against the estimated normal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits claimed only for foreign taxes on income also taxable in South Africa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated normal tax after credits; the basis for first and second provisional payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE tax payable computed in the same manner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable within 6 months of the start of the year; typically 50% of the estimated tax under the basic minimum.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE must make the payment via the same SARS banking details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance payable on or before the last day of the year of assessment; must bring cumulative provisional payments to at least 90% of actual liability (or 100% for SBCs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE must meet the same top-up requirement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: s213 TAA penalty of 10% of the unpaid port of the provisional tax; interest at the prescribed rate; s214 TAA underestimation penalties if the estimate is deliberately or negligently too low; accountability applies to the public officer and directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final dividend withholding tax (DWT) under s64E of the Income Tax Act, levied on the gross amount of any dividend paid by a South African resident company to non-resident beneficial owners, subject to exemptions and treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the South African company (withholding agent), before the dividend payment date: (1) a completed DTD declaration ('Declaration by Beneficial Owner in respect of Dividends') and (2) a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction covering the year of payment. The declaration and TRC may be lodged via SARS eFiling or in hard copy; the company must withhold at 20% until valid documents are held and must retain the records for 5 years. Reduced rates are typically 5% for direct investment (≥10% voting power) and 15% for portfolio holdings under most South African DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory withholding under s49B, commonly reduced to 5%-10% under DTAs (e.g., 10% under the South Africa-China and South Africa-United Kingdom DTAs). Interest: 15% statutory withholding under s37A, commonly reduced to 0%-10% under DTAs (e.g., 10% under most treaties; 0% for government debt or where the DTA expressly exempts). Treaty relief requires TRC plus a DTD/interest-royalty declaration before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 100 million in aggregate cross-border connected-person transactions in a year of assessment triggers mandatory preparation and retention of a Master File and Local File (effective for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2016). Country-by-Country (CbC) Report is required only where the multinational group's consolidated annual turnover equals or exceeds ZAR 10 billion.
